Issues.Title: fix(upgrade): only compile the template contents of a downgraded component
Issues.Body:
Previously, a downgraded component compiled whatever its element contained when the component was created. By then, AngularJS could already have linked or written content into the element, for example through `ng-transclude` or `ng-bind` on it, and that content was compiled again.

The contents are now copied when the directive's controller is instantiated, before anything on the element is linked, and that copy is what gets compiled. If there is nothing to copy, whatever AngularJS put into the element is projected as it is, so content added by `ng-transclude` keeps the scope it was linked with.

Fixes #71441
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(upgrade): only compile the template contents of a downgraded component" (#71442)

Issues.Title: `downgradeComponent()` compiles content that AngularJS directives wrote into its element
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? upgrade ### Is this a regression? No ### Description When a downgraded component is created, [`compileContents()`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/v22.2.3/packages/upgrade/src/common/src/downgrade_component_adapter.ts#L68-L83) compiles whatever is inside its element at that moment, not only the original template: ```ts const projectableNodes: Node[][] = this.groupProjectableNodes(); // this.element.contents() const linkFns = projectableNodes.map((nodes) => this.$compile(nodes)); ``` The directive is [`terminal`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/v22.2.3/packages/upgrade/src/common/src/downgrade_component.ts#L126-L129), but with priority 0, so other priority 0 directives on the same element still run. If one of them already wrote a value into the element, that value is compiled as an AngularJS template, and a `{{ }}` in the data runs as an expression. AngularJS itself takes transcluded content when the template is compiled, before any binding runs, so the same templates are inert without the downgraded component. In the examples the value is only bound as data, nothing passes it to `$compile`. The payload is ```text `{{constructor.constructor('alert(document.domain)')()}}`. ``` I found two ways the content gets there first. **1. With `downgradeModule()`, the component is created after the module bootstraps** ```html

``` `UserBadgeComponent` only has ``. It is created once the Angular module [bootstraps](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/v22.2.3/packages/upgrade/src/common/src/downgrade_component.ts#L243-L245), and by then `ng-bind` already wrote the name into the element. This affects every downgraded element linked before the module is ready, like all the items of an `ng-repeat`. Elements linked later are fine. An Angular app that lazy loads AngularJS, like the ["Lazy Loading AngularJS"](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/16.2.12/aio/content/guide/upgrade.md?plain=1#L614-L697) example, bootstraps both on every navigation to that route, so it happens on every visit. `ng-bind-html` works the same way and doesn't even need `{{ }}`. `$sanitize` keeps ``, and [`ngBind` is `restrict: 'AC'`](https://github.com/angular/angular.js/blob/v1.8.3/src/ng/directive/ngBind.js#L56), so filtering `{{` out of the data doesn't help. With `UpgradeModule` the component is created while the element is linked, before `ng-bind` writes anything, so these values stay text. **2. With `ng-transclude` on the element, also with `UpgradeModule`** A wrapper that forwards its content to a downgraded component: ```js .directive('profileCard', () => ({ transclude: true, template: '', })) ``` ```html {{u.name}} ``` `ngTransclude` and `appCard` both have priority 0, so AngularJS [sorts them by name](https://github.com/angular/angular.js/blob/v1.8.3/src/ng/compile.js#L3750-L3755) and runs their post-link functions [in reverse](https://github.com/angular/angular.js/blob/v1.8.3/src/ng/compile.js#L3370-L3371). `ngTransclude` appends the linked content first, and then `compileContents()` compiles it again, which the AngularJS compiler guide calls [double compilation](https://github.com/angular/angular.js/blob/v1.8.3/docs/content/guide/compiler.ngdoc#L383-L389). In AngularJS 1.8.3, `ng-href` and `ng-src` [write their value while linking](https://github.com/angular/angular.js/blob/v1.8.3/src/ng/directive/attrs.js#L424-L426), so a `{{ }}` in `u.website` runs. With `UpgradeModule` this needs a component name that sorts before `ngTransclude`. With `downgradeModule()` any name works on the first render, and even a plain `href="{{u.website}}"` runs. An `` inside the element throws `ngTransclude:orphan` ([#44753](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/44753)), so the attribute is how a wrapper can forward its content to a downgraded component. | Template | `downgradeModule()` | `UpgradeModule` | Without the downgraded component | | -------------------------------------- | ------------------- | --------------- | -------------------------------- | | `ng-bind` on the element | alert | no alert | no alert | | `ng-bind-html` on the element | alert | no alert | no alert | | `ng-transclude` + `ng-href` / `ng-src` | alert | alert | no alert | | `ng-transclude` + plain `href="{{ }}"` | alert | no alert | no alert | ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug See https://github.com/SkyZeroZx/angular-upgrade-ng-bind-xss, one app per case. ### Anything else? I don't have much experience with `@angular/upgrade`, so maybe I'm missing something. But I think this is a security issue. The [upgrade guide](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/16.2.12/aio/content/guide/upgrade.md?plain=1#L224-L226) says that on a downgraded element "you can apply additional AngularJS directives to it, but _not_ Angular directives", and the AngularJS [security guide](https://github.com/angular/angular.js/blob/v1.8.3/docs/content/guide/security.ngdoc#L35-L36) says "If an attacker has access to control AngularJS templates or expressions, they can exploit an AngularJS application via an XSS attack". Here plain data ends up compiled as a template.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "`downgradeComponent()` compiles content that AngularJS directives wrote into its element" (#71441)

Issues.Title: fix(compiler-cli): prevent static members from clobbering same-named instance inputs/outputs
Issues.Body:
Follow-up to https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/71427.

Scopes `reject_static_member_io` and `process_decorators` in `extract_inputs_outputs` to the current class element's entries and skips recording `static` members in `MemberIo.members`. Previously, a static member with the same name as an instance input/output could wipe out the instance member's metadata, leak its pending decorator options, or bind metadata-declared inputs to the static member.

Without this change, `test_instance_io_not_clobbered_by_same_named_static_member` fails because:
- `static readonly metaInput = 1` is recorded in `MemberIo.members` ahead of instance `metaInput = 2`, causing `bind_to_member` to mark the metadata-declared `inputs: ['metaInput']` entry as `is_restricted: true`.
- `static foo = 2` (after `@Input() foo = 1`) and `static bar() {}` (after `@Output() bar: any`) cause `reject_static_member_io` to drain the earlier instance entries from `out.fields`.
- `@Input(REMOTE_OPTS) static baz = 'unrelated'` (before `baz = input(1)`) leaves its `MemberIoOptions` in `out.pending_options`, which `fold_member_options` then applies to the instance `baz` input (`alias: Some("staticAlias"), required: true` instead of `None, false`).
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(compiler-cli): prevent static members from clobbering same-named instance inputs/outputs" (#71436)

Issues.Title: zone.js: CommonJS Promise.all ignores Set inputs and resolves prematurely
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

zone.js

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

In `zone.js@0.16.3`, loading Zone.js through CommonJS causes `Promise.all()` to ignore promises supplied in a `Set`. It fulfills with an empty array, including when the input contains a pending promise.

This caused intermittent database migration test failures in an application using RxDB, which passes a `Set` of pending writes to `Promise.all()`.

### Minimal reproduction

Tested with Node.js `v24.22.0`:

```sh
npm install zone.js@0.16.3

node -e 'require("zone.js"); Promise.all(new Set([Promise.resolve(1)])).then(console.log)'
```

**Expected:** `[1]`  
**Actual:** `[]`

The same expression produces the expected result with native Promises and with Zone.js loaded through `import('zone.js')`.

### Investigation

The published `bundles/zone.umd.js` contains this loop inside `ZoneAwarePromise.allWithCallback`:

```js
for (var _i = 0, values_3 = values; _i < values_3.length; _i++) {
```

Since a `Set` has no `.length` property, the loop skips its elements.

The [TypeScript source](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/zone.js-0.16.3/packages/zone.js/lib/common/promise.ts#L451) uses `for…of`. However, the separate [ES5 compilation commands](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/zone.js-0.16.3/packages/zone.js/tools/zone_bundle.bzl) omit `--downlevelIteration`.

Compiling the working bundle with those options reproduces the failure. Adding `--downlevelIteration` preserves iterable handling and fixes the reproduction.

```

```true

```

Issues.Body:
…ith Navigation API

When a traversal navigation is redirected by a guard or resolver, NavigationPrecommitController.redirect() cannot be used because redirect() is only valid for push and replace navigations per the WHATWG Navigation API spec (calling it on a traversal throws InvalidStateError).

To match existing History API behavior, the traversal is allowed to commit first (transitioning to the traversal entry), and then the Router initiates a replace navigation to the redirect destination.

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): align NGP ExpressionPrinter formatting with ngtsc TS printer
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Resolves the `TODO(ngp-parity)` in `packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/testing/src/ngp_emit_normalizer.ts` by aligning NGP's `ExpressionPrinter` (`packages/compiler-cli/preprocessor/src/output_ast_printer.ts`) with `ngtsc`'s TypeScript AST printer (`ExpressionTranslatorVisitor` + `TypeScriptAstFactory`) and removing the corresponding AST/regex post-processing hacks from test normalizers:

1. **Operator-precedence-aware parenthesization (`EmitterVisitor`)**:
   - Tracks `AssignmentExpression`-permissive positions (top-level `ExpressionPrinter.print()`, `ExpressionStatement`, `ReturnStatement`, `DeclareVarStmt` initializer, `IfStmt` condition, call/new/comma-separated argument lists, array/object/template literal elements, spread expressions, index accesses, arrow concise bodies, and ternary branches) via `withUnparenthesized()`.
   - Uses JS/TS operator precedence, associativity, and `??`/`&&`/`||` mixing rules (`canOmitBinaryOperandParens`) to omit redundant parentheses on `BinaryOperatorExpr`, `ConditionalExpr`, and `UnaryOperatorExpr` while preserving explicit `ParenthesizedExpr` nodes and required precedence/associativity grouping.
2. **Single-line `FunctionExpr` formatting & argument comma spacing**:
   - Formats `FunctionExpr` nodes whose body is a single `ReturnStatement` without leading comments on a single line (`function(...) { return ...; }`), matching `TypeScriptAstFactory.createFunctionExpression`.
   - Separates comma-delimited expression lists with `', '` in `visitAllExpressions`.
3. **Test normalizer cleanup (`ngp_emit_normalizer.ts`, `expect_emit.ts`, `compliance_spec.ts`)**:
   - Removes `stripRedundantClarifyingParens`, `transformOutsideStringLikeTokens`, Prettier re-formatting in `compliance_spec.ts`, and the ad-hoc parenthesization/factory/comma regexes from `normalizeNgpEmitForComparison` and `normalizeNgpOutputFile`.
   - Canonicalizes single-quoted string literals inside `${...}` template literal interpolations (such as `$localize` placeholder expressions) in `canonicalizeStringQuotes`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "refactor(compiler-cli): align NGP ExpressionPrinter formatting with ngtsc TS printer" (#71432)

Issues.Title: fix(router): keep navigation synchronous when no route resources are used
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

When `withRouterResources()` is enabled on a router configuration, the navigation pipeline runs `setupAndRunResources` between `createRouterState` and route activation (`ActivateRoutes`).

Every other stage in `navigation_transition.ts` short-circuits synchronously (`of(t)`) when there is no asynchronous work to perform, and `switchTap` is designed to stay synchronous (`return of(v)`) when its callback returns `undefined`. However, `setupAndRunResources` unconditionally returns `Promise.all(resourceSetupPromises).then(() => Promise.all(blockingResourcePromises))`—even when no routes in the transition define `resources` and both arrays are empty.

Because a `Promise` is always returned to `switchTap`, enabling `withRouterResources()` globally forces `switchTap` into its asynchronous `from(nextResult)` path on every navigation, deferring route activation and navigation completion by two microtask ticks after guards and resolvers finish. This breaks existing application and test code that relies on navigation completing synchronously once a guard or resolver emits (for example, in `fakeAsync` tests where a `Subject`-backed `canActivate` guard or `resolve` function emits after the initial `NavigationStart` microtask has been flushed, or when router events/state are inspected synchronously right after resolving a guard/resolver).

### Minimal Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-3eywta1r

The StackBlitz runs a `fakeAsync` test that initiates `router.navigateByUrl('/target')` guarded by a `Subject<boolean>`, flushes the initial `NavigationStart` microtask (`flushMicrotasks()`), and then synchronously emits and completes `guard$` before asserting `router.url === '/target'`:

1. **Default (`USE_WITH_ROUTER_RESOURCES = false`, `APPLY_FIX = false`)**: The test passes (`router.url === '/target'`).
2. **Uncomment `USE_WITH_ROUTER_RESOURCES = true`**: Enabling `withRouterResources()` (even though the `/target` route has no `resources`) causes the test to fail with `FAIL: Expected router.url to be '/target', but got '/'` because `setupAndRunResources` defers activation behind an unawaited microtask chain.
3. **Uncomment `APPLY_FIX = true`**: With the empty-promise check in `setupAndRunResources`, `switchTap` remains synchronous and the test passes again.

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

`setupAndRunResources` returns early (`undefined`) when both `resourceSetupPromises` and `blockingResourcePromises` are empty, allowing `switchTap` to take its synchronous `of(v)` branch and preserving synchronous navigation completion after guards and resolvers when no route resources are involved.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

## What is the current behavior?

When two component instances have identical hydration annotations, the server dedupes them into one `ngh` entry, so on the client they share the same serialized object. `prepareI18nBlockForHydrationImpl` calls `shift()` on the ICU case queue from that object, so the first instance empties it and the second one finds no active case. Its server-rendered ICU nodes are never claimed and the content is rendered twice (or throws `expected matching nodeType` in dev mode).

Issue Number: #71425

## What is the new behavior?

The case queue is copied before it is consumed, so every instance reads the full serialized queue and the ICU hydrates correctly.

Issues.Title: i18n hydration: ICU content is duplicated when several component instances share the same `ngh` hydration data
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? core ### Is this a regression? No ### Description With `provideClientHydration(withI18nSupport())`, an ICU expression (`plural`) is rendered twice after hydration when the same component appears more than once on a page and the instances have identical hydration annotations (same structure and same active ICU case). SSR output (correct): ```html
21 modelos
...
19 modelos
``` DOM after client hydration (production build): ```html
21 modelos
...
19 modelos19 modelos
``` The first instance hydrates correctly. Every later instance that shares the same `ngh` index gets duplicated ICU content. In a development build, the same page throws during hydration instead: ``` ERROR Error: ASSERTION ERROR: expected matching nodeType [Expected=> 8 == 3 <=Actual] ``` #### Root cause 1. On the server, `SerializedViewCollection.add()` (`packages/core/src/hydration/annotate.ts`) deduplicates serialized views by `JSON.stringify`. Both component instances therefore get the same `ngh="N"`, and the case queue for the ICU (`"l": {"": [1]}`) is serialized only once. 2. On the client, `retrieveHydrationInfoImpl()` (`packages/core/src/hydration/utils.ts`) assigns `data = nghData[Number(nghAttrValue)]` without copying it. Embedded views do the same in `locateDehydratedViewsInContainer()` (`data: serializedView`). Every instance with the same `ngh` gets **the same object**. 3. `prepareI18nBlockForHydrationImpl()` (`packages/core/src/hydration/i18n.ts`) takes that shared array and **mutates** it: ```ts const caseQueue = hydrationInfo.data[I18N_DATA]?.[index - HEADER_OFFSET] ?? []; // ... const selectedCase = state.isConnected ? context.caseQueue.shift() : null; ``` The first instance calls `shift()` and empties the shared array. For the second instance `caseQueue.shift()` returns `undefined`. No ICU case is treated as connected, so the server-rendered text nodes of the active case are never claimed and the client renders the case again next to them. In dev mode the hydration cursor is then on the wrong node, which triggers the `nodeType` assertion. The same thing happens when the views are repeated by a `MULTIPLIER` (`"x"`), because those views also share the serialized object. #### Suggested fix Do not mutate the serialized data, for example: ```ts const caseQueue = [...(hydrationInfo.data[I18N_DATA]?.[index - HEADER_OFFSET] ?? [])]; ``` Alternatively, consume the queue with an index instead of `shift()`. #### Workaround Replace the ICU with control flow and separate i18n messages: ```html @if (count === 1) { 1 item } @else { {{ count }} items } ``` ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug Minimal setup (SSR + `provideClientHydration(withI18nSupport())`): ```ts @Component({ selector: 'app-count', template: ` @if (count) { {count, plural, =1 {1 item} other {{{count}} items}} } `, }) export class CountComponent { @Input() count = 0; } @Component({ selector: 'app-root', imports: [CountComponent], template: ` `, }) export class AppComponent {} ``` ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug _No response_ ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```true ERROR Error: ASSERTION ERROR: expected matching nodeType [Expected=> 8 == 3 <=Actual] (dev mode only; in production the ICU content is silently duplicated) ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```true Angular: 18.2.14 (application builder, SSR prerendering, compile-time localization) The same code is unchanged in 19.2.25, 20.3.34, 21.2.25, 22.2.3 and 22.3.0-next.2. ``` ### Anything else? _No response_

Issues.Title: fix(common/http): fall back to raw values when HttpParams decoding fails
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist
- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type
- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?
`new HttpParams({fromString: window.location.search})` throws an uncaught `URIError: URI malformed` when the query string contains malformed percent-encoding (e.g. `%ZZ`), aborting `HttpParams` construction. The documented usage with `window.location.search` makes this reachable from crafted URLs (shared links, navigation, reload), causing availability loss. In-repo precedent `parseCookieValue` already falls back to the raw value on decode failure; `URLSearchParams` is likewise tolerant. Only `paramParser` propagates the exception.

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?
Decoding is attempted per key/value inside try/catch; on failure the raw key/value is kept (same fallback shape as `parseCookieValue`). Normal percent-encoding (`%20`, UTF-8) is unaffected. Verified with a Node reproduction: 9/9 malformed inputs threw before, 0/9 after; 4/4 control inputs unchanged.

Note: AI tools (OpenCode + Muse Spark) assisted with code search, patch drafting and PoC scripts; all output was reviewed and verified with executable reproductions by the author.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?
- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## What is the current behavior?

`ResourceImpl` keeps its `AbortController` after a load resolves and calls `abort()` with no reason when the resource is destroyed. Issues.Title: fix(forms): safely chain debounced async validation resources
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [X] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [X] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [X] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features): API docs/JSDocs updated

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [X] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

In signal forms, `validateAsync` with `debounce` configured passes a params signal that can throw the internal `ResourceParamsStatus.LOADING`. Factories that consume that signal in an effect or use `resourceFromSnapshots` can fail outside the `resource()` params handler.

The `ɵchain` function seems only used in that way in signal forms (`ɵchain(` has only 1 result in the codebase), and [the docs mention](https://angular.dev/guide/signals/resource#chaining-resources) that chain is to be used on the params function, giving the consumer the option to chain resources, while the `validateAsync` function hides that and can lead to unexpected errors when the param function throws in an unexpected context. That creates a problem for libraries that can return the Resource interface but don't use the Resource API, since it's the Resource API param's function that catches the issue, not the Interface that libraries can implement to adapt into Angular libraries.

Issue Number: #70884

## What is the new behavior?

Pass a safe debounced params signal to the factory, retaining the previous value during debounce, and compose the debounce resource and factory resource safely, without `ɵchain`. The safe chain forwards reloads to preserves `reloadValidation()` functionality.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [X] No

## Other information

In the future, a resource type that declares the `Resource & { reload: () => boolean }` could be used as a union to better declare the usage of the reload method, see https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/69443 (alternatives considered for `validateAsync` interface) and  https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/71299 (Router's `nonBlocking` utility type).

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): consolidate initial shared chunks into main with Rolldown
Issues.Body:
When esbuild bundles an application with lazy-loaded routes, modules that are statically reachable from the main entry point and also imported by different subsets of lazy routes are split into separate shared chunks, often forming multi-level import chains from main.js. Previously, the Rollup-based chunk optimization pass recognized that the main entry point is always loaded before any dynamic import can execute and merged all modules in its static closure back into main.js.

After switching chunk optimization to Rolldown, unconfigured Rolldown only merged direct single-hop shared chunks into main.js while leaving deeper initial shared chunks as separate files. Configuring Rolldown with preserveEntrySignatures set to allow-extension and a codeSplitting group targeting the built-in $initial tag restores the consolidation of all initial shared modules into the main entry chunk while keeping lazy-only shared chunks separate.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(@angular/build): consolidate initial shared chunks into main with Rolldown" (#34408)

Issues.Title: refactor(@angular/build): extract shared breadth-first initial file analysis
Issues.Body:
Previously, both `BundlerContext` and `optimizeChunks` maintained separate implementations for discovering transitive initial files and calculating their import depths from the esbuild metafile. Both implementations used a depth-first stack traversal via `Array.prototype.pop()`, which visited deeper branches in reverse import order and failed to propagate updated minimum depths to the transitive dependencies of already-visited chunks in diamond dependency graphs.

This commit extracts a shared `findTransitiveInitialFiles` helper that uses a breadth-first queue traversal over direct static imports. Processing chunks in breadth-first order guarantees that each file is discovered at its true shortest import depth on first visit, preserves the natural declaration order of imports at each depth level, and eliminates the duplicated metafile traversal logic across initial bundling and chunk optimization.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "refactor(@angular/build): extract shared breadth-first initial file analysis" (#34407)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): invalidate Vite module cache for removed dev server output files
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check to confirm your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: N/A

Lazy and shared chunks are named after their content hash (`chunk-[hash].js`), so a rebuild that changes a chunk gives it a new name, along with any hashed chunk that imports it. The incremental build result reports the old names in `removed`.

In `dev-server/vite/index.ts`, removed files are only deleted from `generatedFiles` and `assetFiles`. Their entries in Vite's module graph are never invalidated. Updated files are invalidated by `invalidateUpdatedFiles` in `hmr.ts`, but removed names are no longer in `generatedFiles` by then, and Vite's own file watcher is disabled, so nothing cleans them up.

As a result:

1. The transformed code and source map of every renamed chunk stay in memory until `ng serve` is restarted. Memory grows with each save that renames chunks.
2. A request for an old chunk URL is answered from the stale cache with `200` and outdated code instead of `404`.

To reproduce: an app with three lazy routes that import one ~210 KB shared module. Edit the shared module 25 times. After each rebuild, request the new chunks as a reloading browser would, then force GC. Each save renames 4 chunks.

| | `@angular/build` 22.2.3 | This PR (`pnpm build --local`) |
|---|---|---|
| Heap after GC, 25 saves | 46.6 → 59.0 MB (~508 KB per save) | 47.0 → 47.9 MB (~37 KB per save) |
| Vite module-graph entries holding a transform result | 6 → 106 | 6 → 6 |
| Cached code + source maps | 4.42 → 15.97 MB | 4.42 → 4.42 MB |
| Request for an old chunk URL | 200 (stale code) | 404 |

The leak per save scales with the size of the renamed chunks and their source maps, so apps with large shared chunks lose more.

## What is the new behavior?

For each removed output file, the matching Vite modules are looked up and invalidated, the same way `invalidateUpdatedFiles` already does for updated files. This releases their cached transform results. Requests for old chunk names now return `404`.

The new spec `serve-renamed-chunks_spec.ts` loads a lazy chunk, edits the lazy module so the rebuild renames the chunk, and checks that the old URL returns `404`. It fails without this change (`Expected 200 to be 404.`) and passes with it.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

- Template-only HMR updates don't produce removed files (`build-action.ts` clears them on that path), so they are not affected by the leak or by this change.
- `invalidateModule` clears the cached transform result but leaves the module node in Vite's maps. That is the remaining ~37 KB per save in the table above. Removing the nodes entirely would need more than invalidation. I kept this change minimal, but I'm happy to extend it if you prefer.
- With SSR, Vite's module runner keeps its own evaluated-module cache, which this change doesn't touch.

The `web-worker` schematic adds `webWorkerTsConfig` to the options of the project's `test` target, regardless of which builder that target uses. New applications use the `@angular/build:unit-test` builder, whose schema does not have a `webWorkerTsConfig` option, so `ng test` fails schema validation afterwards. The option is still needed on the `build` target (where the schematic also adds it). Removing it from the `test` target makes `ng test` pass again, including with the worker in place. Relevant code: `packages/schematics/angular/web-worker/index.ts` if (testTarget) { (testTarget.options ??= {}).webWorkerTsConfig ??= workerConfigPath; } ### Minimal Reproduction 1. `ng new ww-repro --defaults` 2. `cd ww-repro` 3. `ng test --watch=false` → passes 4. `ng generate web-worker app` 5. `ng test --watch=false` → fails with the error below After step 4, the `test` target in `angular.json` is: "test": { "builder": "@angular/build:unit-test", "options": { "webWorkerTsConfig": "tsconfig.worker.json" } } Deleting `webWorkerTsConfig` from the `test` target options makes `ng test` pass again. ### Exception or Error ```text Error: Schema validation failed with the following errors: Unknown option "webWorkerTsConfig". Valid options are: buildTarget, tsConfig, runner, runnerConfig, browsers, browserViewport, include, exclude, filter, watch, headless, debug, ui, isolate, splitting, quiet, coverage, coverageInclude, coverageExclude, coverageReporters, coverageThresholds, coverageWatermarks, reporters, outputFile, providersFile, setupFiles, progress, listTests, dumpVirtualFiles. ``` ### Your Environment ```text Angular CLI : 22.2.3 Node.js : 24.15.0 Package Manager : npm 11.12.1 OS : darwin arm64 @angular/build : 22.2.3 vitest : 5.0.5 ``` ### Anything else relevant? Suggested fix: only add `webWorkerTsConfig` to the `test` target when it uses a Karma builder (`@angular-devkit/build-angular:karma` / `@angular/build:karma`). The unit-test builder gets build options from its `buildTarget`. Happy to send a PR with a spec.

Issues.Title: fix(@schematics/angular): skip `webWorkerTsConfig` for unit-test builder test targets
Issues.Body:
The `web-worker` schematic added the `webWorkerTsConfig` option to the project's `test` target regardless of its builder. Issues.Title: `ng new --view-encapsulation` has no effect on generated components
Issues.Body:
### Command

new

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

The `--view-encapsulation` option of `ng new` / `ng generate application` is documented as "Sets the view
encapsulation mode for components in the initial project", but it currently has no effect:

1. The root `App` component is generated without `encapsulation`, so its styles stay scoped (Emulated).
2. The value is not saved to the project's `@schematics/angular:component` defaults in `angular.json`, so components
   generated later with `ng g c` also use Emulated.
3. For `--no-standalone` apps, `main.ts` gets `bootstrapModule(AppModule, { defaultEncapsulation: ViewEncapsulation.X })`.
   `defaultEncapsulation` is only read by the JIT compiler, so it has no effect with AOT, which is the default for
   `ng build` and `ng serve`.

This looks like #13689 again: it was fixed in 89797900db by setting the encapsulation on the root component and in
`bootstrapModule`, but the root component part was removed in 58bc5b8f2a (for #13742, invalid generated code), leaving
only the JIT-only option.


### Minimal Reproduction

1. `ng new ve-repro --defaults --view-encapsulation=None` (same result with `--no-standalone`)
2. Add `h1 { color: red; }` to `src/app/app.css`
3. `ng build --configuration development`
4. The output contains `h1[_ngcontent-%COMP%]`, i.e. the styles are still encapsulated.
5. `angular.json` has no `viewEncapsulation` under `projects.ve-repro.schematics`, so `ng g c foo` also generates an
   Emulated component.


### Exception or Error

```text

```

### Your Environment

```text
Latest
```

### Anything else relevant?

Possible fix: set `encapsulation` on the generated root component, save `viewEncapsulation` in the component schematic
defaults, and drop `defaultEncapsulation` from `main.ts`. Happy to send a PR.

Issues.Title: fix(@schematics/angular): apply `viewEncapsulation` to generated application components
Issues.Body:
The `viewEncapsulation` option of the application schematic had no effect. The root component template did not set `encapsulation`, the value was not added to the component schematic defaults, so components generated later used the default encapsulation, and the `defaultEncapsulation` option added to `bootstrapModule` in `main.ts` for NgModule applications is only used by the JIT compiler.

Set `encapsulation` on the root component, add `viewEncapsulation` to the component schematic defaults in `angular.json`, and remove the ineffective `defaultEncapsulation` option from `main.ts`.

Fixes #34388

Issues.Title: ng update: "Package '@angular/core' is not a dependency" in a bun workspace member
Issues.Body:
### Command

update

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

20.3.40

### Description

In a bun workspace where the Angular project is a workspace member (not the root package), `ng update <package>` cannot find any of the project's dependencies:

```
$ bunx ng update @angular/core
Using package manager: bun
Collecting installed dependencies...
Found 1 dependencies.
Package '@angular/core' is not a dependency.
```

The same layout behaves differently by CLI version (checked today with bun 1.4.3):

- 20.3.40: `Found 20 dependencies`, then `Package '@angular/core' is already up to date.`
- 21.2.27: `Found 1 dependencies.` then `Package '@angular/core' is not a dependency.` (`ng update` without arguments still lists the packages)
- 22.2.3: same failure. This also blocks `ng update @angular/core@22 @angular/cli@22` from 21, since the temporary 22 CLI fails the same way.

#32787 fixed this for npm workspaces (#34308). The bun path has no equivalent, and on `main` it is unchanged:

- `listDependenciesCommand` for bun is `['pm', 'ls']`. Run from the member's directory, it prints the root's dependencies, that is the workspace members themselves:

  ```
  /tmp/repro node_modules (405 installed)
  └── app@workspace:app
  ```

- `parseBunDependencies(stdout, logger)` does not use the `{ workspacePackageName }` options that `#populateDependencyCache` passes. It returns that single entry, so every requested package is "not a dependency".

#32781 reported this for bun (same layout) and was closed as a duplicate of #32787, but the npm fix does not cover it.

Since `bun pm ls` has no per-member output, one possible direction is to build the member's dependency map from its `package.json` and the installed manifests. The `migrateOnly` path already falls back to that through `findPackageJson`.

### Minimal Reproduction

```sh
mkdir repro && cd repro
printf '{ "name": "root", "private": true, "workspaces": ["app"] }\n' > package.json
bunx @angular/cli@22.2.3 new app --skip-git --skip-install --package-manager bun --defaults --interactive=false --ssr=false --ai-config=none
bun install
cd app
bunx ng update @angular/core
```

### Exception or Error

```text
Using package manager: bun
Collecting installed dependencies...
Found 1 dependencies.
Package '@angular/core' is not a dependency.
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.2.3
Node.js           : 24.21.0
Package Manager   : bun 1.4.3
Operating System  : darwin arm64
```

### Anything else relevant?

Workaround: update the versions with bun (`bun add @angular/core@^22.2.3 …`), then run each package's migrations with `ng update <package> --migrate-only --from=<old> --to=<new>`. That path does not depend on the dependency list.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "ng update: "Package '@angular/core' is not a dependency" in a bun workspace member" (#34402)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): only load autocompletion in interactive shells
Issues.Body:
Previously, `ng completion` appended an unconditional `source <(ng completion script)` statement to the user's shell configuration file. When non-interactive shells (such as those spawned by scripts, automation tools, or coding agents) sourced the configuration file, they still paid the overhead of starting Node.js and generating the completion script despite tab completion not being used.

This change wraps the `source <(ng completion script)` command in an `if [[ $- == *i* ]]; then` check so that autocompletion is only loaded when the shell is interactive, and updates the manual setup documentation accordingly.

Closes #34307

## What is the current behavior?

## What is the new behavior?

The import map now skips only entry points and files that actually received a hint, so all other initial chunks are covered. New specs fail before the change and pass after it.

Issues.Title: Allow index.preloadInitial to preload the full static closure of the initial bundle (number or "all")
Issues.Body:
### Command

build

### Description

#27581 limited modulepreload hints to a shallow set of 10 initial chunks, as a safe default for all applications (#27490). For an application with a deep initial import graph that default costs one network round trip per depth level: the browser only discovers the chunks at depth N after the chunks at depth N-1 have arrived and been parsed.

Our `main` has a static closure of 45 chunks across six depth levels. We post-process `index.html` after `ng build` to preload all of them. Measured in production RUM over three weeks (roughly a million initial loads per week), weekdays before versus after:

| Segment | LCP p75 before | LCP p75 after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| all initial loads | 2.00 s | 1.84 s |
| effective connection type 4g, desktop | 2.07 s | 1.91 s |
| effective connection type 3g, desktop | 7.0 s | 5.3 s |
| effective connection type 2g, desktop | 22.8 s | 14.7 s |

The slowest connections gained the most, which is the opposite of what the HTTP Archive correlation cited in #27490 would predict. That correlation covers preloads of any resource. Chunks in the entry point's static closure are all required before the application can execute at all, so preloading them does not compete with anything more critical than the stylesheet.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Let `index.preloadInitial` accept a number or `"all"` in addition to the current boolean, keeping `true` as today's shallow-10 behaviour. That would let us delete a post-build script that has to track the CLI's `index.html` output, and which broke on the `integrity` attributes added in 22.x.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Post-processing `index.html` (what we do now); setting `preloadInitial: false` and writing every hint ourselves (same fragility); eager-loading the landing route into the main bundle (adds 330 KB gzipped to every first load for the 70% of visits that land elsewhere).

Issues.Title: subresourceIntegrity leaves initial chunks beyond the modulepreload cap without any integrity metadata
Issues.Body:
### Command

build

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

With `subresourceIntegrity: true`, the application builder covers the emitted JavaScript in three places:

1. the entry scripts (`main`, `polyfills`) and the stylesheet get an `integrity` attribute;
2. up to `MODULE_PRELOAD_MAX` (10) initial chunks get a `<link rel="modulepreload">` carrying `integrity`;
3. every other `.js` output goes into the integrity-only `<script type="importmap">`.

Step 3 skips initial files on purpose (`index-html-generator.ts`: `if (!file.path.endsWith('.js') || initialFiles.has(file.path)) continue;`), on the assumption that step 2 carries their hash. But step 2 is capped at 10, sorted by depth. Any initial chunk past the cap is therefore hashed nowhere: it is loaded through a static `import` from `main` with no integrity check, even though SRI is enabled.

In our application `main`'s static closure is 45 chunks. A production build hashes 10 of them in preload tags and 0 in the import map, leaving 34 initial chunks without integrity metadata. The import map has 451 entries, all of them lazy chunks.

### Minimal Reproduction

Any application whose initial bundle splits into more than 10 chunks, built with `"subresourceIntegrity": true` in the production configuration:

```sh
ng build --configuration production
grep -o 'integrity="sha384-[^"]*"' dist/<app>/browser/index.html | wc -l   # tags
ls dist/<app>/browser/chunk-*.js | wc -l                                     # emitted chunks
```

Diff the chunk names present in `index.html` (tags plus the import map's `integrity` keys) against the chunks in the output directory. The chunks statically imported by `main` at depths beyond the first 10 preloads appear in neither.

### Exception or Error

```text
No error. The chunks load without an integrity check.
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.2.2
Node.js           : 24.20.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.19.0
@angular/build    : 22.2.2
@angular/core     : 22.2.1
OS                : macOS (local), Linux (CI)
```

### Anything else relevant?

Expected: every emitted chunk is covered either by a tag or by the import map. The simplest fix seems to be dropping the `initialFiles.has()` exclusion for initial chunks that did not receive a preload tag, or including every chunk in the import map. A chunk hashed in both places is harmless, since both hashes must match the same file.

### [`v12.14.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.14.0): pnpm 12.14.0

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.13.0...v12.14.0)

This release adds the `sideEffectsCache.exclude` setting, stops `pnpm install` from waiting on the daily update check, and keeps pnpm from aborting with a core dump when the reader of its output exits.

##### Minor Changes

- Added the `sideEffectsCache.exclude` setting for packages whose build depends on something pnpm cannot include in the cache key, such as the system libraries a native addon links against. pnpm builds the listed packages in every project and never restores or saves their builds through the side-effects cache, locally or on a `remoteCache` server. Under the global virtual store, each project gets its own copy of these packages and of the packages that depend on them. Entries use the same `name`, `@scope/*`, and `name@version` patterns as `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` [#​5271](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/5271).

- `pnpm login` now prints the `npm-notice` response header during web-based login. Registries use it to show the verification code that completes the sign-in in the browser.

##### Patch Changes

##### Installing packages

- `pnpm install` and `pnpm add` no longer wait for the daily update check. If the command finishes first, pnpm skips the update notice and checks again next time. On a registry that accepted the connection but never answered, an install that had nothing to do used to take minutes [#​16839](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16839).

- `pnpm install`, `pnpm add` and `pnpm update` now reuse `pnpm-lock.yaml` when the workspace configures a catalog entry that no dependency references, such as an unused entry or one whose package an `overrides` entry replaces. Before, every resolution in such a workspace resolved all dependencies again from the registry [#​16923](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16923).

- `pnpm install` now looks up a git dependency's branch or tag once per install, even when many workspace projects depend on it. With `linkWorkspacePackages` enabled, it used to run `git ls-remote` once per project [#​16899](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16899).

- A filtered install, such as `pnpm install --filter <pkg>`, now keeps the `pnpm-lock.yaml` entries of workspace projects that are missing from disk, as in a sparse checkout. Their importers, packages, and catalog entries stay even when the filter matches every project on disk [#​16931](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16931).

- pnpm now decides whether a dependency that a package also declares as an optional peer is linked as a dependency or as a peer from the shallowest path that reaches the package. When an existing lockfile records such a dependency as a regular dependency and a newly added dependency now provides the peer, pnpm records it as a peer, as a fresh install does. The lockfile entry of such a package can change on the next install [#​16901](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16901).

- An install that adds nothing to the store no longer changes the modification time of the store directory. CI caches that check modification times, such as GitLab's, no longer re-upload an unchanged store [#​16929](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16929).

##### Running commands and scripts

- pnpm no longer aborts with a core dump when the reader of its output has exited, as in `pnpm list | head -1` or `pnpm start 2>&1 | head -1`. The command finishes with its usual exit code, and a failing script's exit code is kept. A write to stdout that fails for another reason, such as a full disk, ends the command with exit code 1 [#​16904](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16904) [pnpm/tasks#132](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/132).

- On Windows, `pnpm exec`, `pnpm run`, and commands such as `pnpm nx` now return when the command they run exits, even if it left a detached process running and pnpm's output is redirected or piped. Previously a shell reading that output waited until the detached process, such as the Nx daemon, exited [#​16930](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16930).

- Commands that do not write the project manifest now leave a missing `package.json` absent. This covers queries such as `pnpm why` and `pnpm outdated`, `pnpm fetch`, `pnpm dedupe --check`, and commands that exit with an error, such as `pnpm rt ls`. These commands used to create one from the initialization template. `pnpm sbom` run from a lockfile alone now reports the root component as `unknown` with version `0.0.0` [#​16907](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16907).

- `pnpm run` now reports a failed script as a JSON record under `--reporter=ndjson`. It printed a plain `[ELIFECYCLE]` line to stderr.

- `pnpm run` no longer prints `[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code N.` to stderr when a script fails under `--reporter=silent`, `--silent`, or `--loglevel=silent`.

- `pnpm pipeline --dry-run` no longer writes a run report when no projects are selected. With `--json` it prints `{"tasks": []}` [pnpm/tasks#126](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/126).

##### Packing and publishing

- `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now ship the whole gitignored directory that `main`, `browser`, or `bin` points into, as npm does. Previously only the `main` and `bin` files themselves were packed, and a gitignored `browser` file was left out [#​16908](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16908).

- `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now honor a `.npmignore` or `.gitignore` inside a subdirectory when `package.json` has a `files` field. The package root's ignore files and those inherited from the workspace are still skipped [#​16909](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16909).

##### Setting up pnpm and toolchains

- `--registry`, `--https-proxy`, `--http-proxy`, and `--no-proxy` now apply when pnpm resolves and downloads the pnpm version a project pins in `packageManager`. Before, these lookups went to `https://registry.npmjs.org/`, which a firewall that only allows a private registry blocks [#​16911](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/discussions/16911).

- On Windows, `pnpm install` now installs the Rust toolchain for rustup's default host, so a machine set up with `rustup set default-host x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` gets the MinGW toolchain. Without a default host, pnpm installs the MSVC toolchain for the machine's architecture, as rustup does. This includes a pnpm built for MinGW, such as the MSYS2 package, which has installed the MinGW toolchain since 12.13.0. An x64 pnpm on ARM64 Windows now installs the ARM64 toolchain [#​16854](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16854).

### [`v12.13.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.13.0): pnpm 12.13.0

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.12.1...v12.13.0)

This release adds the `pnpm profile` and `pnpm token` commands, the `storeIndexFormat: files` setting for stores shared over a network filesystem, and faster Python dependency resolution.

##### Minor Changes

- Added the `pnpm profile` command to view and update registry user profile settings.

- Added `pnpm token` to list, create, and revoke authentication tokens on the registry.

- Added the `storeIndexFormat` setting. Set it to `files` to keep a store's package index as one file per package instead of the SQLite `index.db`, for a store on a network filesystem that several machines use at once. SQLite's locking does not work across machines, so concurrent installs on such a store could corrupt `index.db`.

- Added the `nodePackageMap` setting, which groups the package-map settings. `nodePackageMap.mode: write-only` writes `node_modules/.package-map.json` for other tools without making Node.js load it. `mode: load` also makes Node.js load the map, like `nodeExperimentalPackageMap: true`. `nodePackageMap.type` replaces `nodePackageMapType`. The old settings still work [#​14937](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14937).

  ```yaml
  nodePackageMap:
    mode: write-only
    type: loose
  ```

##### Patch Changes

##### Setting up pnpm

- `pnpm setup` now works when pnpm was installed with npm on macOS. It installed pnpm from npm's `bin` directory and left a `$PNPM_HOME/bin/pnpm` that could not run [#​16855](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16855).

- pnpm runs again after `pnpm setup` when `globalShims` enables pnpm. Every command failed with "the global target of the pnpm shim points back at the shim" [#​16874](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16874).

- A pnpm built for the MinGW target on Windows, such as the MSYS2 package, now installs the MinGW Rust toolchain that `rust-toolchain.toml` names. It used to install the MSVC toolchain.

##### Installing packages

- On macOS, `pnpm install` no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_WRITE_FILE` when the project is on a virtiofs or SMB share. pnpm now falls back to a regular `fsync` when the file system rejects a full sync [#​16846](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16846).

- On macOS, `pnpm install`, `pnpm patch-commit`, and other commands that load a pnpmfile no longer hang at random.

- `pnpm install` now puts the executables of a Python build backend's requirements on the `PATH` while the backend runs. Projects built with `uv_build` now install. Before, they failed with "uv-build was not properly installed".

- Removing a `link:` dependency now also removes its symlink from `node_modules` when `nodeLinker` is `hoisted` [#​16884](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16884).

- `pnpm-lock.yaml` no longer records the tarball URL of a package installed from a scoped registry, such as one set by `@types:registry=`, when pnpm can rebuild the URL from that registry [#​16866](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16866).

##### Packing, auditing, and pipelines

- `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now pack only `package.json`, the README, the license, and the files named in `main` and `bin` when `files` is an empty array. They used to pack every file in the package [#​16889](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16889).

- `pnpm audit` and `pnpm audit signatures` no longer check runtimes installed through `devEngines.runtime`, such as `node@runtime:24.21.0`, against the npm package of the same name. `pnpm audit signatures` reported these runtimes as having an invalid registry signature [#​16869](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16869).

- `pnpm pipeline` now runs the root's tasks when `pnpm-workspace.yaml` lists only the root in `packages` or omits `packages`, as `pnpm -r run` does. A change to a root file in such a workspace no longer triggers a full-run warning. When a full run has no projects to run, `pnpm pipeline` now reports that no projects are selected [#​16849](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16849).

##### Performance

- `pnpm install` resolves Python dependencies faster. With `--lockfile-only`, a project with 10 dependencies now resolves in about 4 seconds, down from about 40. When the index publishes a metadata file beside each wheel (PEP 658), as PyPI does, pnpm downloads only the wheels of the releases it selects.

- A repeat install against an existing lockfile no longer reads registry metadata for the dependencies it takes from that lockfile. On a warm store this removes thousands of metadata lookups from a repeat install of a large workspace.

- `pnpm install` with `enableModulesDir: false` now verifies the packages already in the store while the dependencies resolve, and checks a package's files in parallel. On a 5,100-package install with the store on a network filesystem, this removed a 19-second pause between resolution and fetching.

This release adds OIDC authentication to `pnpm dist-tag` and the `tool:` protocol. `pnpm publish` now checks which registry an `NPM_ID_TOKEN` was issued for before using it.

##### Patch Changes

- `pnpm publish` now uses an `NPM_ID_TOKEN` only if its `aud` claim matches the selected registry, such as `npm:registry.npmjs.org`. A token for another registry is skipped with a warning, and pnpm falls back to the configured credentials.

- `pnpm dist-tag add`, `rm`, and `ls` now support OIDC authentication in CI. Enable "Allow npm dist-tag" in the package's trusted publishing settings to manage tags without a stored npm token.

- Added the `tool:` protocol for the tools pnpm downloads itself: Node.js, Bun, Deno, and Yarn. `pnpm add bun@tool:1.3.0`, `pnx node@tool:22`, and `pnx yarn@tool:4` work like the `runtime:` spelling, which stays supported as an alias. A lockfile written for `runtime:` stays up to date when `package.json` switches to `tool:`, and the other way around.

  A named registry can no longer be called `tool`.

### [`v12.12.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.12.0): pnpm 12.12.0

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.11.2...v12.12.0)

This release shares task results and dependency builds through a remote cache, adds the `addMissingPeerTypes` setting, and lets `pnpm add --config` and `pnpm update` manage configuration dependencies. It also fixes `dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds` running the build scripts of packages that `allowBuilds` denies.

##### Minor Changes

- `pnpm pipeline` can share task results between machines. A result is a signed artifact stored on a pnpr server or on a server that speaks the Turborepo Remote Cache API, such as Vercel Remote Cache.

  The remote side-effects cache can also store dependency builds on a Turborepo Remote Cache server. Both caches read the new `remoteCache` setting, which names the server and holds the signing keys. `pnpm pipeline --report` records the run under the organization `remoteCache.org` names.

- Added the `addMissingPeerTypes` setting, which links the `@types` package of a peer dependency next to every package that peer-depends on it. For example, a package that peer-depends on `react` gets the project's `@types/react` linked next to it. This lets TypeScript find the types of a peer dependency when the global virtual store is on [#​15689](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/discussions/15689).

- `pnpm add --config` and `pnpm update` now handle configuration dependencies the way they handle other dependencies [#​16814](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16814).

  `pnpm add --config` saves a version range in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` by the same rules as `pnpm add`, so `pnpm add --config my-config@latest` saves a range such as `^1.2.0`. It also resolves the package again when `pnpm-lock.yaml` already locks an older version.

  `pnpm update` updates configuration dependencies within their ranges, and `pnpm update --latest` moves them to their latest version. A selector such as `pnpm update my-config` updates only the configuration dependencies it names.

##### Patch Changes

- A package set to `false` in `allowBuilds` no longer runs its build scripts when `dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds` is `true`. The two settings together now allow every build except the denied ones. Previously, `dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds` ignored the denials.

- pnpm now switches to the pnpm version a project pins even when it cannot read its configuration. Previously, a setting it rejected in the global config file, an `.npmrc` file, or `_auth`, or a `pnpm-workspace.yaml` it could not parse, stopped every command, `pnpm --version` included.

- `pnpm update` and `pnpm why` accept `--depth Infinity` again. They failed with `invalid value 'Infinity' for '--depth <DEPTH>'` [#​16817](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16817).

- `pnpm deploy` without `injectWorkspacePackages` now binds a peer dependency of a linked workspace package to the version its parent provides, as an injected install does. Previously the deploy failed with `ERR_PNPM_DEPLOY_AMBIGUOUS_PEER` whenever other packages in the deployed graph depended on different versions of that peer [#​16807](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16807).

- `pnpm deploy --legacy` no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_SPEC_NOT_SUPPORTED_BY_ANY_RESOLVER` when a workspace dependency of the deployed project declares a `workspace:` peer dependency that the project does not depend on itself. pnpm now copies that peer from the workspace into the deploy directory.

  An auto-installed peer declared with `workspace:` now always resolves to the workspace project. Previously, `workspace:*` and `workspace:^1.0.0` peers could be installed from the registry [#​16806](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16806).

Issues.Title: unit-test: browser-mode runs stall ("iframe did not become ready") when a Docker container starts alongside
Issues.Body:
### Command

test

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

With `"browsers": ["chromiumHeadless"]` and `@vitest/browser-playwright`, `ng test` stalls in roughly 4 runs of 10 when a Docker container starts while the tests start up. That is what happens when another package of a workspace runs integration tests with Testcontainers at the same time. A few test iframes load Vitest's runtime and never request the Angular test setup (`init-testbed.js`) or their spec chunks; after 60 s the run fails.

On a fresh `ng new` app with six generated components:

| | runs | stalled |
|---|---:|---:|
| `ng test` | 15 | 0 |
| `ng test` with `docker run -d alpine:3 sleep 8` starting beside it | 47 | 21 |
| plain Vitest browser mode (no Angular builder), seven trivial files, same container | 11 | 0 |

The last row (on Vitest 5.0.4; the others on 5.0.4 and 5.0.5 alike) is why I am filing it here rather than with Vitest. Ruled out on the same machine: CPU load (all 16 cores busy), synchronous disk writes, touching a source file mid-run, the image or a published port (`alpine sleep` is enough), and the headless shell itself (the full Chromium build stalls too, less often). Chromium logs no failed request and no console error, and a page opening ~1000 fresh connections to localhost while a container starts loses none.

With `DEBUG=vitest:browser:*`, all seven sessions connect to the tester API at the same moment, then only two send their first command (`__vitest_viewport`); the other five stay silent until the 60 s timeout. A Vite request trace (`DEBUG=vite:time`) of a stalled run shows those five iframes fetched `index`, `plugins` and `rolldown-runtime` from the optimized deps and nothing after; a passing run goes on to `init-compiler.js`, `init-testbed.js`, the Angular deps and the spec files.

It may be the same family as vitest-dev/vitest#11171 (a rejected import inside the tester iframe never fires `iframe.onerror`, so the orchestrator waits until the timeout), closed there for want of a reproduction.

### Minimal Reproduction

```sh
npx @angular/cli@22.2.3 new ng-docker-stall --defaults --skip-git --ssr=false --style=css
cd ng-docker-stall
for c in alpha bravo charlie delta echo foxtrot; do npx ng g c "$c"; done
npm install -D --save-exact vitest@5.0.5 @vitest/browser-playwright@5.0.5 playwright@1.64.1
npx playwright install --only-shell chromium
npx ng config projects.ng-docker-stall.architect.test.options.browsers '["chromiumHeadless"]'
npx ng test    # passes
```

Then, with Docker running, this script, `./stall.sh 10`:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# Runs `ng test` several times while a Docker container starts beside it, and
# counts the runs whose test iframes stall.
runs=${1:-5}
stalled=0
for i in $(seq 1 "$runs"); do
  (id=$(docker run -d alpine:3 sleep 8); sleep 9; docker rm -f "$id" > /dev/null) &
  if npx ng test 2>&1 | grep -q 'did not become ready'; then
    stalled=$((stalled + 1))
    echo "run $i: stalled"
  else
    echo "run $i: passed"
  fi
  wait
done
echo "$stalled of $runs runs stalled"
```

Expected: every run passes, as without the container. Actual: some runs stall and fail after 60 s.

### Exception or Error

```text
⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯ Unhandled Error ⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯
Error: Failed to run the test /…/ng-docker-stall/src/app/echo/echo.spec.ts.
 ❯ process.processTicksAndRejections node:internal/process/task_queues:104:5
Caused by: Error: The iframe "__vitest_all__" did not become ready within 60000ms. The tester likely failed to initialize, check the browser console for errors.

Angular           : 22.2.3
Node.js           : 24.22.0

Issues.Title: bug(material/menu): menu restores focus to its trigger after a menu item opens a dialog (animations disabled / prefers-reduced-motion)
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

 When a mat-menu item opens a MatDialog and animations are disabled (provideNoopAnimations / animations disabled, or the user's OS has reduced motion so `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` matches), the dialog ends up with no focus: focus is moved back to the menu trigger behind the dialog's backdrop.

Cause: with animations disabled the dialog's initial focus runs synchronously during the menu item's click (in the microtask after the click listener). The click then reaches the menu panel, which emits `closed('click')`, and `MatMenuTriggerBase._destroyMenu` calls `this.focus(this._openedBy)` unconditionally, without checking where focus currently is. With animations enabled the dialog focuses ~150ms later, after the menu has closed, so the problem doesn't show.

Since `prefers-reduced-motion` comes from an OS setting (e.g. Windows "Animation effects" off), regular users hit this, and keyboard and screen-reader users land on a control hidden behind the modal.

This was reported in #14879, which was closed as a duplicate of #11696 before the reporter clarified it only happens with NoopAnimationsModule; it was then locked. The menu code on `main` still restores focus unconditionally.

Possible fix, following the dialog's own guard from #17300 ("don't move focus if it was moved during close animation"): in `_destroyMenu`, when the close reason is `'click'`, skip restoring focus if it is already inside a different overlay pane (not the menu's own pane, not a menu panel such as a submenu, and not the overlay pane that contains the trigger itself). Every other close (Escape, Tab, backdrop click, programmatic close) keeps today's
behaviour. This doesn't change the accessibility position in #11696: focus still returns to the trigger whenever the menu owns it; it only stops the menu from pulling focus out of a modal that an item just opened. Happy to send a PR with tests if this direction is acceptable.

### Reproduction

  StackBlitz (from #14879, older Angular/Material):
  https://stackblitz.com/edit/checkbox-reactive-2zhjpp?file=app%2Fapp.component.ts

  I wasn't able to save a new StackBlitz, so this links the reproduction from #14879. The bug is not specific to that
  old version:

  - It reproduces on Angular 21.2.25 / @angular/cdk + @angular/material 21.1.2 in an application with animations
  disabled through the OS setting (Windows "Animation effects" off, so `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` matches and
  Material disables its animations). After a menu item opens a MatDialog, `document.activeElement` is the menu trigger
  behind the dialog's backdrop, not the dialog's `cdkFocusInitial` button.
  - The cause is unchanged on `main`: `MatMenuTriggerBase._destroyMenu` in `src/material/menu/menu-trigger-base.ts`
  still ends with

      if (this.restoreFocus && (reason === 'keydown' || !this._openedBy || !this._triggersSubmenu())) {
        this.focus(this._openedBy);
      }

    with no check of where focus currently is, so whenever the dialog takes focus before the menu finishes closing
  (always the case with animations disabled), the menu takes it back.

  Steps (old StackBlitz, which uses NoopAnimations):
  1. Open the StackBlitz and click the menu trigger.
  2. Click the menu item that opens the dialog.
  3. In the console, run `document.activeElement`: it is the menu trigger, not the dialog's button.

  Single-file reproduction for current versions (Angular/Material 21; paste as main.ts in a new Angular project):

  import {Component, inject} from '@angular/core';
  import {bootstrapApplication} from '@angular/platform-browser';
  import {MatButtonModule} from '@angular/material/button';
  import {MatMenuModule} from '@angular/material/menu';
  import {MatDialog, MatDialogModule} from '@angular/material/dialog';

  @Component({
    imports: [MatButtonModule, MatDialogModule],
    template: `
      <mat-dialog-content>Delete this item?</mat-dialog-content>
      <mat-dialog-actions>
        <button mat-button mat-dialog-close cdkFocusInitial>Cancel</button>
        <button mat-button [mat-dialog-close]="true">Delete</button>
      </mat-dialog-actions>
    `,
  })
  export class ConfirmDialog {}

  @Component({
    selector: 'app-root',
    imports: [MatButtonModule, MatMenuModule, MatDialogModule],
    template: `
      <button mat-button [matMenuTriggerFor]="menu">Menu</button>
      <mat-menu #menu="matMenu">
        <button mat-menu-item (click)="open()">Open dialog</button>
      </mat-menu>
    `,
  })
  export class App {
    private dialog = inject(MatDialog);
    open() { this.dialog.open(ConfirmDialog); }
  }

  bootstrapApplication(App);

  On 21, emulate reduced motion (DevTools > Rendering > "Emulate CSS media feature prefers-reduced-motion: reduce", then
  reload) or set the OS animation setting off, then click Menu > Open dialog and check `document.activeElement`.

### Expected Behavior

Focus stays on the dialog's initial focus target (the "Cancel" button with cdkFocusInitial), showing its focus indicator, exactly as it does when animations are enabled. The menu should not move focus back to its trigger while an overlay opened by the menu item holds focus.

### Actual Behavior

The dialog opens, but focus is on the menu trigger ("Menu") behind the dialog's backdrop: document.activeElement is the trigger button with cdk-focused / cdk-mouse-focused. The dialog shows no focused control, Enter re-activates the hidden trigger, and Tab starts from outside the dialog. The dialog's FocusTrap did focus "Cancel" first; the menu's _destroyMenu then called focus() on the trigger. 

document.activeElement after the dialog opens: button.mat-mdc-menu-trigger  (the menu trigger, behind the backdrop)

### Environment

  - Angular: 21.2.25
  - CDK/Material: 21.1.2 (the same unconditional restore is still in src/material/menu/menu-trigger-base.ts on main)
  - Browser(s): Chrome <your version>; also reproduced in an embedded Chromium. Any browser with animations disabled or
  prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
  - Operating System: Windows 11 (Settings > Accessibility > Visual effects > Animation effects: Off)

The `ngTabPanel` and `ngAccordionPanel` directives warn in dev mode that they need `ngTabContent` or `ngAccordionContent` to render, but content placed directly in a panel already renders. It's created eagerly and stays in the DOM, and the panel gets the `inert` attribute while hidden.

Issues.Title: fix(material/datepicker): update parse error with signal forms when value stays null
Issues.Body:
Fixes #33740.

When a datepicker input is bound to a signal form with `[formField]`, the `matDatepickerParse` error goes stale whenever the model value stays `null`:

- typing an unparseable value (e.g. `foo`) into an empty input does not add the error;
- erasing an unparseable value does not clear it, so the form stays invalid on an empty field (the case in the issue).

## Cause

Signal forms compute the errors of a CVA's legacy validators in a `computed` that re-runs when the control value changes or when the validator calls its `registerOnValidatorChange` callback. In `MatDatepickerInputBase._onInput()`, the `null` to `null` path calls `_cvaOnChange(null)`, which signal forms ignore because the value did not change, and it never calls `_validatorOnChange()`: that call was only in the branch for a non-null, unchanged date. Reactive forms don't hit this, because `setValue` always re-runs the validators.

## Fix

Call `_validatorOnChange()` whenever the parse state flips while the value stays the same, including `null` to `null`. The branch that already did this for an unchanged non-null date behaves as before.

With reactive forms, the `null` to `null` case with a changed parse state now also triggers `updateValueAndValidity()` after the `setValue(null)` call. It gives the same result, with one extra `valueChanges`/`statusChanges` emission in that case.

## Testing

Two tests in `datepicker.spec.ts` use a real signal form (`form()` + `FormField`). Both fail on `main` and pass with this change:

- typing `foo` into an empty input sets `matDatepickerParse`;
- setting a date, typing `foo`, then clearing the input removes it.

`//src/material/datepicker:unit_tests_chromium` (407 tests, including the date range input) and `//src/material/input:unit_tests_chromium` pass locally.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(material/datepicker): update parse error with signal forms when value stays null" (#33951)

Issues.Title: build: fix API docs extraction of directives and imported types
Issues.Body:
The ARIA and CDK API pages on angular.dev are missing information, because the API extraction can't resolve several imports:

- 8 aria directives are shown as classes, and their inputs and outputs as plain properties, because their host directives are imported from another package.
- The drag-drop target doesn't use the import map, so `@angular/core` doesn't resolve, and its imports of other cdk packages aren't available. Most of its directives and its NgModule are shown as classes, and their inputs and outputs as plain properties.
- Many types are shown as `any`.

The extraction doesn't report any of this, because it ignores Angular compilation errors.

## Changes

Extraction rule:
- Map an import map entry to its target's own entry point, and fail if it doesn't exist. Currently, the rule picks the shortest `index.d.ts` among the target and its dependencies, which maps `@angular/aria/private` to `src/cdk/platform/index.d.ts`.
- Resolve relative imports of files outside `srcs` to the type declarations among the inputs, by setting `rootDirs` to include the bin directory. This mirrors how `ts_project` sees sources and declarations. A new `deps` attribute provides declarations that the import map doesn't.
- Map wildcards of directory entries relative to the directory itself, so that subpath imports like `rxjs/operators` resolve.
- Treat missing compiled stylesheets as empty, since they aren't inputs of the action and don't affect the docs.
- Fail on Angular compilation errors.

Targets: all of them use the wrapper with the import map, and those with relative imports of other packages (aria, drag-drop and three cdk/testing targets) get `deps`.

## Effect on the generated docs

Compared with `main`, 46 of the 110 aria and cdk API pages change:
- 13 classes are shown as directives and one as an NgModule, and their inputs and outputs as such, e.g. `readonly id = input<string>()` instead of `readonly id: InputSignal<any>`, or `@Input('cdkDragData') data: T` instead of `data: T`.
- Types shown as `any` show their real type, e.g. `Signal<boolean>` instead of `Signal<any>`, or `Subject<{ source: DragRef<any>; event: MouseEvent | TouchEvent; }>` instead of `any` for `DragRef.started`.
- Members inherited from base classes that now resolve are listed.
- The `Combobox` page no longer links `DeferredContentAware` to `/api/aria/private/DeferredContentAware`, which doesn't exist.

No page or member is removed, and no type gets worse. The remaining `any`s are declared as such in the source.

## Testing

- Every docs target builds on `main` and on each commit. Comparing all fields of the generated JSON, each commit only changes what its message describes.
- Each fix is needed: removing it brings its errors or `any`s back. Moving the remaining cdk/testing targets to the wrapper and removing the unused import map entry don't change the output, and neither does the stricter entry point for the remaining import map entries, which already resolve to their own entry point.
- `bazel build //...`, `pnpm lint` and the aria/combobox unit tests pass.
